title: eRNA Extraction from Water Samples Using NucleoMag DNA/RNA Water Kit
author: Marine Vautier
materials: In this step, the buffers provided by the kit are distributed in a 96-well plate. For RNA extraction from filtered water samples, the 12 columns of the plate are divided into 2 sections of 6 columns each, allowing up to 16 samples to be extracted per plate. Annotate the 96-well plate as recommended below: Table 1: Recommended plaque annotation Note: It is useful to mark the dividing line between columns 6 and 7 with a marker pen to provide a visual cue for filling the plate. Add the appropriate buffers into the appropriate wells of the plate (Table 2): 1 st column / 7 th column: Will be filled during plate preparation 2/2 2 nd column / 8 th column: 850 µL of MWA3 (1 st wash) 3 rd column / 9 th column: 850 µL of MWA3 (2 nd wash) 4 th column /10 th column: Will be filled during plate preparation 2/2 5 th column / 11 th column: 850 µL of MWA4 (3 rd wash and bead drying) 6 th column / 12 th column: 50 µL or 65 µL of RNase-free H 2 O (RNA elution) Note: The choice of elution volume is based on the expected eRNA amount. The smaller the amount, the smaller the elution volume in order to obtain more concentrated RNA. Table 2 : Plate preparation 1/2 Film and reserve the plate at Room temperature

steps.title: Aliquot buffers and decontaminate scissors
steps.instruction: Aliquot kit buffers to avoid contamination: place MWA1, MWA2, MWA3 and MWA4 into 50 mL tubes; place NucleoMag B‑Beads solution and RNase‑free H₂O into 2 mL tubes. Annotate tubes as follows – one 2 mL tube per sample for lysate collection, one 5 mL tube per eight samples for the NucleoMag B‑Beads + MWA2 mix preparation, and three 0.5 mL tubes per sample for RNA collection. Prepare three 50 mL tubes containing (i) RNA‑removing solution (e.g., RNase‑Off), (ii) molecular‑biology‑grade water, and (iii) ethanol. Decontaminate scissors before the protocol and between each filter cutting by dipping the scissors sequentially into the three tubes, opening and closing the scissors in each tube.

steps.title: Reconstitute and dilute rDNase
steps.instruction: Add 4 mL reaction buffer to the lyophilized rDNase vial, incubate 2–3 min at room temperature, and gently shake to dissolve (avoid vigorous mixing). Transfer the reconstituted rDNase to a 50 mL tube, add 28 mL reaction buffer, and gently shake. The resulting solution is sufficient for 96 samples; if fewer samples are processed, aliquot the rDNase (do not freeze‑thaw more than three times) and store aliquots at –20 °C for at least six months.

steps.title: Prepare MWA2 mix (no beads)
steps.instruction: Prepare one 5 mL tube for up to eight samples (plan for one extra sample; e.g., mix for nine if extracting eight). Add only MWA2 buffer to the tube (volumes per Table 4, not reproduced here). Do not add NucleoMag B‑Beads at this stage.

steps.title: Mechanical and chemical lysis of filters
steps.instruction: Collect the 5 mL tubes containing frozen filters and keep them on ice. Immediately add 750 µL MWA1 buffer to each tube, then cut the filter into small pieces directly in the tube using decontaminated scissors (decontaminate scissors between each sample as described in step 1). Vortex vertically for 5 seconds at median speed, then vortex horizontally for 5 minutes at maximum speed. Transfer the tubes to a benchtop centrifuge, spin, and pipette the lysate (~650 µL) into a labeled 2 mL tube. Centrifuge the 2 mL tube at 11 000 × g, °C, for 30 seconds. Keep the tubes at room temperature until they are distributed into the 96‑well plate.

steps.title: Prepare bead‑lysate plate
steps.instruction: Vigorously vortex the NucleoMag B‑Beads tube. For each tube of MWA2 buffer prepared in step 3, add the volume of NucleoMag B‑Beads specified in Table 4 and vortex to mix. Remove the film from the 96‑well plate. Add to wells in columns 4 and 10: 500 µL of the NucleoMag B‑Beads + MWA2 mix, then 450 µL of lysate (supernatant from the 2 mL tubes). Slowly agitate the rDNase mix tube (prepared in step 2) and add 300 µL of rDNase mix to wells in columns 1 and 7.

steps.title: Run RNA extraction part 1
steps.instruction: Place the plate into the MagnetaPure 32 system and insert the magnetic‑rod cover (see instrument manual). Select the program “RNA extraction part 1” (Table 6) and start the run (≈ 35 minutes). At the end of the DNA‑digestion step, remove the plate and add 350 µL MWA2 buffer to wells in columns 1 and 7.

steps.title: Run RNA extraction part 2
steps.instruction: Place the plate back into the MagnetaPure 32 system (magnetic‑rod cover need not be changed). Select the program “RNA extraction part 2” (Table 8) and start the run (≈ 30 minutes).

steps.title: Post‑run handling and storage
steps.instruction: After the run, remove the plate and place it on ice in the DNA/RNA workstation. Remove the magnetic‑rod cover and initiate UV decontamination according to the instrument manual. Transfer each eRNA extract into a pre‑annotated 0.5 mL tube (aliquot directly to avoid freeze‑thaw cycles). Optionally measure RNA concentration and quality (e.g., Nanodrop). Store the eRNA extracts at –80 °C.
